html:
The El Mozote massacre was the killing of about 800 people, many of them children, by an army battalion in and around the village of El Mozote in northeastern El Salvador in December 1981.

The Atlacatl Battalion, newly trained by the United States, swept the area looking for guerrillas of the civil war. In El Mozote the soldiers separated the men, women and children and killed nearly all of them over two days, then burned the village. The village had been seen as neutral.

American reporters described it in early 1982, but the governments of El Salvador and the United States denied it. Forensic teams digging in 1992, after the peace accords, found the bones of children. An amnesty law blocked trials until the Supreme Court struck it down in 2016. It is the best-known atrocity of the Cold War in Latin America.
sum: The El Mozote massacre was the killing of about 800 people, many of them children, by an army battalion in and around the village of El Mozote in northeastern El Salvador in December 1981.
